guide.title: How Airlock works
guide.sub: The method behind the app, plus a replayable tour.
guide.tourDesc: Five stops through a real session: nav, problems, editor, submit, techniques.
tour.s1b: Train holds the work, Track holds progress, Manage holds setup.
tour.s2b: Open the list and pick A+B, the sanity-check problem.
tour.s3b: Fill the analysis scaffold, then write the solution below it.
tour.s4b: Run checks quietly, Submit logs the verdict in the console below.
tour.s5b: Mark techniques Learning or Assimilated as you reassess them.
checklist.title: First week
practice.notesPlaceholder: Write your approach after solving. It sticks for your juniors and for you.
practice.autosavedHint: Autosaved to the problem. Visible next time you open it.
practice.noCompilerDetails: No details. You can try compiling locally with g++ -O2 -std=c++17.
practice.compileHint: For C++ make sure you include bits and use correct syntax. For Java the file must contain
practice.whitespaceHint: Hint: comparison ignores trailing spaces per line. Check newlines.
practice.tleHint: Did not finish in time. Look for infinite loops or O(n²).
practice.approachConfirm: Level 7 may show the approach, possibly with code. Reveal it?
contest.setupSub: Configure once, race the clock, upsolve after.
contest.name: Contest name
contest.teamMembersLabel: Team members comma separated, 3 for ICPC
contest.noPastContests: No past contests yet. Run one and it will appear here.
contest.upsolveBanner: Time is up. You are now upsolving. Submissions are tagged as upsolve and do not affect the live scoreboard.
contest.pickProblem: Pick a problem from the sidebar
stress.title: Stress test lab
stress.description: Fuzz your solution against a brute force. Generator takes seed from argv[1] and prints one test case. Candidate and brute read from stdin.
stress.idleHint: Fill the three editors and click Run. Start with the templates.
stress.mayTakeSeconds: This may take a few seconds
stress.agreeHint: Generator and both solutions agree. Try more cases or a different generator.
stress.copyHint: Copy the input and run both solutions locally to debug. Check whitespace handling.
stress.compileFailed: Stress test failed to compile or run
import.title: Import problems
import.subtitle: Add curated problems while you have internet. Paste the JSON shape from Problem or use the form. Use sample-problems/*.json as template.
import.hintsLabel: Hints, up to 7 (level 7 may contain code)
import.hintPlaceholder: Hint {n} — a question or nudge, not the answer
import.testsNonEmpty: tests must be a non empty array.
import.savedWithTests: Saved "{title}" with {count} tests. It now appears in Practice.
history.title: History and stats
history.subtitle: Every Practice and Contest submission is logged. Filter by tag or verdict, inspect code, track accuracy.
history.confirmClear: Clear all {count} submissions? This cannot be undone. Contests and problems will stay.
history.confirmReset: Reset all data? This will delete all submissions and contests but keep problems. This cannot be undone.
history.noTagged: No tagged submissions yet. Submit in Practice to see breakdown.
history.noMatch: No submissions match the filter. Try submitting a solution.
verdict.Accepted.hint: Your solution produced the correct output for every test case.
verdict.WrongAnswer.description: Your program ran but the output was wrong.
verdict.WrongAnswer.hint: Check the failing test below. Compare your output with the expected one character by character. Watch for extra spaces or missing newlines.
verdict.TimeLimitExceeded.description: Your program took too long and was stopped.
verdict.TimeLimitExceeded.hint: The judge killed it after the time limit. You need a faster algorithm or to fix an infinite loop. Time limit is shown on the problem.
verdict.RuntimeError.hint: This is usually a bad array access, division by zero, null pointer, or out of memory. The error output below may show the line.
verdict.CompileError.hint: Fix the compiler errors below and try again. For C++ check missing semicolons and brackets. For Java the public class must be named Main.
diff.comparisonHint: Comparison is whitespace sensitive except trailing spaces per line are ignored by the judge. Check for missing newlines or extra spaces. Characters highlighted show first difference.
editor.switchConfirm: Switching language replaces the current code. Continue?
editor.resetConfirm: Reset to the template? Unsaved changes will be lost.
tracks.graphs-week1.title: Graphs week 1
tracks.dp-week1.title: DP week 1
tracks.arrays-week1.title: Arrays week 1
tracks.arrays-week1.description: Two pointers → sliding window → prefix sums
failure.question: What kind of miss was this?
techniques.title: Techniques
techniques.subtitle: What you know, stated honestly. After a break, reassess — don't assume retention.
techniques.notesPlaceholder: What does this technique need? When does it apply? What tripped you up?
techniques.empty: No techniques yet. Add the ones you train — e.g. Prefix Sum, Two Pointers.
recall.title: Recall mode
recall.subtitle: Reimplement a technique from memory. No statement, no hints, no notes until you finish.
recall.empty: No techniques yet. Add some in
recall.compareHint: Compare against your own notes, then grade yourself honestly.
recall.noNotes: No notes written for this technique.
set.emptySlot: Nothing fits — add problems or update Techniques.
reimpl.title: Due for reimplementation
journey.title: Journey
journey.subtitle: Recorded progress over time. Suggestions appear here when the data supports them.
journey.suggestionBody: Recent practice and contest records support star {star} ({tier}). Add a note to record it, or leave it for now.
journey.reflectionPlaceholder: What changed in your practice that supports this step?
journey.noSuggestion: No step suggested right now. Continued practice updates this.
onboard.name: Display name
workspace.noResult: Submit a solution to see the result here.
workspace.notesHidden: Notes stay hidden while you reimplement from memory. They return after you submit.
settings.failedHint: Check the connection, that the release is published (drafts do not update), and the signing keys.
workspace.runHint: Run against the tests without logging a submission
import.packDesc: Import a problem pack from disk: pick its pack.json manifest, then the problem files it lists. Techniques merge gently, problems insert or replace.
import.packBadManifest: Manifest is not a valid pack (needs problem_files).
whatsnew.title: What's new in {v}
whatsnew.sub: Updated successfully. Highlights below, full notes on GitHub.
welcome.languageSub: Airlock speaks English and Portuguese. You can switch later in Settings.
welcome.pathSub: Two paths, same vault. Everyone gets the same problems and techniques.
welcome.newbieDesc: Start from zero with the starter vault and your first submit.
welcome.returnerDesc: Rusty is normal. Same vault, then reassess your techniques.
welcome.setupSub: Your name and default code language. Thirty seconds, then you never see this again.
welcome.loadAllSub: {problems} problems and {techniques} core techniques land locally. Offline, no account, yours to keep.
welcome.loadError: Could not load everything. Check the counts and try again.
welcome.doneSub: The vault is loaded. Open a problem and submit — the verdict console shows the rest.
welcome.next1: Submit A+B and read the verdict console
welcome.next2: Try Recall mode on one technique
welcome.next3: Generate a training set in Practice
settings.title: Settings
settings.replayDesc: Clears the onboarding flag and takes you back to the start. Your problems, techniques and history stay untouched.
settings.themesHint: A theme renames and recolors the 8 journey tiers. Your stars and reflections carry over — only names and colors change.
settings.dataDirHint: Linux path shown — equivalent OS app-data folder on Windows/macOS. Back it up by copying the file.
settings.devNote: Updates work in the installed app, not in dev.
